# Data Quality Scorecard

*Generated by `python -m hcls docs` from run `2026-10-21T20:23:18Z` (commit `26d0c9f4`). As-of date 2026-10-21. Do not edit by hand.*

## Headline

- **441 rules** were run across the 19 data tables (every column, every foreign key, every date, plus 39 business rules).
- **164 rules found problems**: 5 Critical, 23 High, 73 Medium, 63 Low (plus 16 'Info' items: fields that are empty by design, such as `denial_reason` on claims that were not denied).

## The three confirmed issues from the brief

| rule_id | issue | rows_failed | rows_checked | pct_failed | first_seen | last_seen |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| C01 | Insurance_Claims.approved_amount | 90 | 250 | 36 | 2020 | 2026 |
| C02 | Visits.appointment_id | 123 | 400 | 30.75 | 2020 | 2026 |
| C03 | Medical_Records.prescribed_meds | 40 | 206 | 19.42 | 2023 | 2026 |


`first_seen` / `last_seen` are the first and last year in which the problem occurs. The same problem appearing in every year points to a design gap, not a recent break (see the root-cause report).

## All Critical and High findings

| rule_id | table | name | severity | rows_failed | rows_checked | pct_failed | impact_statement |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A02 | Insurance_Claims | claim patient differs from the patient on the linked bill | Critical | 250 | 250 | 100 | CRITICAL - claims do not join to the right bill; any claims-to-billing figure (including over-charging) is unreliable. |
| A30 | Prescription_Administration | administration patient differs from the prescription patient | Critical | 400 | 400 | 100 | CRITICAL - a dose is recorded against one patient but the prescription belongs to another; the link is broken. |
| A38 | Patient_Insurance | linked claim belongs to a different patient | High | 230 | 230 | 100 | Insurance record points at someone else's claim. |
| A03 | Insurance_Claims | submitted_amount larger than the linked bill total | High | 244 | 250 | 97.6 | Claimed amounts are far above billed amounts, another sign the claim-to-bill link is wrong. |
| A31 | Prescription_Administration | administered unit differs from prescribed unit | High | 349 | 400 | 87.25 | Dose unit mismatch is a medication-safety risk. |
| C01 | Insurance_Claims | approved_amount missing | Critical | 90 | 250 | 36 | CRITICAL - Finance cannot state approved revenue for these claims; the reconciliation gap cannot be closed. |
| C02 | Visits | appointment_id missing (visit not linked to an appointment) | Critical | 123 | 400 | 30.75 | CRITICAL - patient journey cannot be traced from appointment to visit to bill. |
| A24 | Admissions | discharge_date earlier than admit_date | High | 152 | 289 | 52.6 | Length of stay cannot be computed; bed-day reporting is wrong. |
| A28 | Prescriptions | end_date earlier than start_date | High | 118 | 293 | 40.27 | Prescription duration is impossible; active-medication lists are unreliable. |
| C03 | Medical_Records | prescribed_meds missing (stored as the text "None") | Critical | 40 | 206 | 19.42 | CRITICAL - patient-safety risk; doctors cannot see the medication that was prescribed. |
| A01 | Insurance_Claims | billing_id reused by more than one claim | High | 89 | 250 | 35.6 | One bill is attached to several claims, so claim totals may double count the same charge. |
| A12 | Billing | bill raised for a Cancelled or No-Show appointment | High | 81 | 249 | 32.53 | Patients may have been billed for care that was not delivered. |
| R-Visits-patient_id | Visits | patient_id has no matching Patients.patient_id | High | 45 | 400 | 11.25 | Orphan patient_id: these Visits rows cannot be joined to Patients. |
| R-Medical_Records-patient_id | Medical_Records | patient_id has no matching Patients.patient_id | High | 16 | 206 | 7.77 | Orphan patient_id: these Medical_Records rows cannot be joined to Patients. |

## Cross-check against the workbook's own `Referential_Integrity` sheet

The workbook ships a sheet that lists foreign-key violations. We recomputed each line from the data.

| Admissions | patient_id | Patients | 1 | 1 | 3 | matches |

| Medical_Records | patient_id | Patients | 8 | 8 | 16 | matches |

| Nurses | supervisor_nurse_id | Nurses | 1 | 1 | 2 | matches |
| Patient_Procedures | code_id | Procedure_Codes | 1 | 1 | 5 | matches |

| Patients | hospital_id | Hospitals | 31 | 6 | 81 | sheet over-reports |
| Patients | primary_care_doctor_id | Doctors | 500 | 0 | 0 | sheet over-reports |
| Prescription_Administration | patient_id | Patients | 5 | 5 | 20 | matches |
| Prescriptions | patient_id | Patients | 1 | 1 | 5 | matches |
| Referrals | patient_id | Patients | 2 | 2 | 2 | matches |
| Referrals | referred_doctor_id | Doctors | 1 | 1 | 4 | matches |
| Visits | patient_id | Patients | 5 | 5 | 45 | matches |


**2 line(s) in the sheet do not match the data.** Where the sheet over-reports, the sheet compared text values (for example `'379'`) with numeric ids (`379`), so valid links were counted as violations. The scorecard uses the recomputed numbers (DECISIONS D-010).

## What cleaning fixed (raw vs cleaned data)

The same rules were re-run on the cleaned data. Rules that now pass were fixed by standardisation; everything still failing needs a business or source-system fix and was deliberately **not** altered.

- Format / validity rules fully fixed: **31** of 34 that had failures.
- Total failing cells before cleaning: **16,205**; after: **14,622**.
